newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Apple Fields gains 21 pct after threat.
newsitem.headline: Apple Fields gains 21 pct after threat.

text.p: Apple Fields gained 11 cents, 21 percent, to 63 cents on Wednesday after it made a statement threatening to close its orchards if refused an export licence.
It said it would then become solely a property and investment company.
Brokers said they were somewhat bemused by the rise, describing the buying as speculative, and noted it was on light volume in a stock thinly traded.
"If they rip out all the orchards it won't exactly be bad for them or if they get consent to export then that would be good news as well," said Egden Wignall broker Grant Williamson.

"If they get consent to export then that will be good for the cash flow, and if they can't they will be knocking the expenses on the head and becoming virtually a land holding company with some very good assets," he said.
Williamson said it was known the orchards had not been paying their way and Apple Fields' threat to pull its orchards out at the end of the month would greatly improve a poor cashflow position.
Another Christchurch broker said apple companies were seen as high risk and if Apple Fields became a pure property investment company there would be much less risk.
